To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hemin therapy attenuates renal injury in deoxocorticosterone (DOCA) salt hypertension by reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and extracellular matrix accumulation.
hemin therapy attenuates kidney damage in DOCA-salt hypertension by suppressing the oxidative stress/inflammation and the corresponding decline of extracellular matrix protein synthesis.
the administration of the heme oxygen-ase inducer hemin to deoxycorticosteron-salt hypertensive animals lowered blood pressure and improved kidney function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HO-1 in renal protection in a model of mineralocorticoid hypertension.
the HO system as a therapeutic target for the treatment of end-organ damage.
the role of hemin in the treatment of hypertension-induced kidney damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HO system plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of end-organ damage, and that the induction of the HO system by hemin attenuates kidney injury and improves renal function in DOCA-salt hypertensive animals.
hemin therapy attenuates kidney damage in DOCA-salt hypertensive by upregulating HO system and suppressing the inflammatory/oxidative stress.
HO-1 is an important regulator of kidney damage in DOCA-salt hypertension, and that hemin may be a promising therapeutic agent for the treatment of kidney damage in hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hemin attenuates kidney injury by reducing oxidative and inflammatory damage, and by decreasing fibronectin expression.
hemin therapy is renoprotective in DOCA-salt hypertension by attenuating oxidative/inflammatory insults and by inhibiting the activation of the profibrotic TGF-beta/fibronectin signaling pathway.
the HO system is an important regulator of the renoprotection and the antihypertrrophic actions of hemin in nephrectomy-DOCA-salt hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HO system has the potential to be a new therapeutic approach for the treatment of kidney injury in mineralocorticoids-induced hypertension.
the HO system is a potential therapeutic target to treat end-organ damage.
the HO system has a pivotal role in the regulation of renal function and structure.
